html:
The Zoque are an Indigenous people of western Chiapas and neighbouring Oaxaca and Tabasco in southern Mexico. O' de püt and Angpøn are names they use for themselves in different dialects.

Their languages belong to the Mixe-Zoque family, which many scholars think was spoken by the Olmec, so the Zoque may descend in part from that early civilisation. At the Spanish conquest they lived between the warlike Chiapanecs and the Gulf lowlands. Related peoples include the Mixe of Oaxaca and the Popoluca of Veracruz.

In 1982 the eruption of the El Chichón volcano destroyed several Zoque villages and scattered their people across Chiapas.
